It seems common for many readers to be disappointed in the film versions of the books they have read. Catch-22 and Ragtime are two examples that come to mind immediately of books that really should have never been transferred to screen, either because the pleasure of reading them came from the author's language, or the luxurious development of individual characters. After seeing Ragtime, I vowed I would never watch a movie based on a book I have read.

And yet, I break this rule often. Most recently with Rainer Werner Fassbinder's "World on a Wire" a film based on the novel "Simulacron 3" by Daniel F. GALOUYE.

The problem here is that Galouye's book is a novel of ideas, which Fassbinder transferred into long stretches of dialogue between characters that underscored the fact that the book should never have been made into a movie. Very dissapointing.

So, what films have you seen that didn't measure up to your experience reading the book?

Why?
Which books far excel the movies upon which they are based?

Eragon. Not because the book is good, no; the movie is just absolutely f&%#ing terrible. I walked out of that movie raging about what was wrong with it, and didn't get done talking until four hours later. There is no conceivable universe where anyone thought it was a good idea. It was a money grab, pure and simple.

Characters, like Angela, were changed from quirky and interesting to cliche and boring. Locations were actually scaled down, going from epic to...bland, at best.

They ripped out the heart of the movie, the character development, the epic fantasy landscape, the interesting characters, and replaced it with lightning and bad CG dragons.
